description: Batch C of Mock Exam 6: author AND evaluate 30 original BABOK v3-based CBAP questions (working ids 61-90) as a self-contained unit with a per-batch quality/difficulty evaluation gate before acceptance. THIRD of four batches. Must not duplicate the 1650 existing questions NOR Batches A/B. Coverage focus for Batch C (planned to balance the overall exam): RADD (Requirements Analysis and Design Definition) and Solution Evaluation weighted, plus 2-3 more financial/quantitative calculation items to reach the exam-wide ~7-8 total together with Batch B. Save accepted 30 items to .agents/tasks/task-add-mock6-exam/batches/batchC.json.
steps: Confirm branch add-mock-exam-6 and that batchA.json and batchB.json (30 items each) already exist.
Reuse the dedup corpus builder; corpus = all 1650 existing stems + Batch A + Batch B stems.

Author 30 NEW, original, scenario-driven CBAP questions grounded in BABOK v3 with fresh scenarios, four non-empty A-D options and one defensible answer each, with BABOK-grounded explanations that justify the key and rule out distractors.

Include 2-3 more financial/quantitative calculation items. For EVERY calculation item, write the FULL step-by-step arithmetic in the explanation and verify the numeric result step by step so the keyed letter provably matches the worked computation; fix the keyed answer if the computation disagrees. Coordinate with Batch B so the exam-wide financial total lands around 7-8.
Label a target difficulty per item and calibrate toward ~25% medium / ~50% difficult / ~25% very difficult within the batch.

EVALUATE THE BATCH before accepting (gate): single defensible answer + plausible distractors per item; unambiguous self-contained stems; batch hits ~25/50/25 mix (tally; revise up if drifting easy); explanations rule out distractors; every calculation item's arithmetic matches its keyed letter. Revise weak items until the batch passes.
Dedup the 30 vs existing 1650 + Batches A/B and internally; replace near-duplicates; iterate to 0.
Honesty tag unverifiable specifics with '[verify against your BABOK reference]'.
Save the 30 accepted items as a JSON array to .agents/tasks/task-add-mock6-exam/batches/batchC.json (working ids 61-90; do NOT touch js/data/questions.json yet).

Record findings: achieved difficulty mix, coverage spread, per-batch A/B/C/D tally, worked arithmetic + confirmed answer letter for each financial item in this batch, evaluation-gate pass, dedup 0-duplicates confirmation (vs existing + A + B + internal).
acceptance_criteria: .agents/tasks/task-add-mock6-exam/batches/batchC.json exists and parses as a JSON array of exactly 30 valid question objects.
Per-item difficulty labels tally to roughly 25% medium / 50% difficult / 25% very difficult, recorded in findings.
Every calculation item in this batch has full step-by-step arithmetic and a keyed answer matching the worked computation (recorded in findings).
Batch evaluation gate recorded in findings.
Dedup reports 0 duplicates/near-dupes vs the 1650 existing stems AND vs Batches A/B, and 0 internal duplicates.
js/data/questions.json and js/app.js are NOT modified by this feature.
verification: python3/node: load batches/batchC.json; assert length==30; validate keys, 4 non-empty A-D choices, answer in ABCD, non-empty explanations.
python3/node dedup: corpus = 1650 existing + batchA + batchB stems; assert 0 batchC matches; assert 0 internal duplicates.
Re-derive each financial item's arithmetic and confirm keyed letter matches.
git diff --stat main -- js/data/questions.json js/app.js shows no changes from this feature.
findings:
Batch C complete: 30 original scenario-driven BABOK v3 questions authored, evaluated, and saved as a JSON array to .agents/tasks/task-add-mock6-exam/batches/batchC.json (working ids 61-90). Each item carries the non-schema 'difficulty' key convention from Batches A/B (to be stripped at FEAT-005 compile; production schema is answer/choices/explanation/id/question only). Two reusable validators were added alongside: validate_batchC.py (schema + difficulty tally + answer tally + financial re-derivation) and dedup_batchC_full.py (extends dedup_corpus.py so the corpus = 1650 existing + Batch A + Batch B stems). js/data/questions.json and js/app.js were NOT modified (git diff --stat vs main shows no changes to either file). Confirmed on branch add-mock-exam-6; batchA.json and batchB.json (30 items each) and dedup_corpus.py already present and reused.

ACHIEVED DIFFICULTY MIX: medium=8 (27%), difficult=15 (50%), very difficult=7 (23%) -> hits the ~25/50/25 target. First draft drifted EASY (medium=10 / difficult=18 / very difficult=2). The evaluation gate caught this and, rather than relabel arbitrarily, I promoted seven items that genuinely require the finest discrimination to 'very difficult' (id63 Verify-vs-Validate distinction; id65 requirement/design continuum framing; id67 reconciling requirements with a design constraint via value trade-off; id72 solution-limitation vs enterprise-limitation source; id82 interpreting variance against acceptable-range tolerance; id78 benefit-cost-ratio equal-net-benefit trap; id86 diagnosing an enterprise (not solution) limitation) and promoted two recall-style mediums to 'difficult' (id73 recommend-actions purpose among plausible options; id83 outcome-vs-output benchmark). Final tally recomputed and verified programmatically.

COVERAGE SPREAD (Batch C weighting per plan = RADD / Requirements Analysis and Design Definition (KA5) + Solution Evaluation (KA6), complementing Batch A's KA1/KA2 and Batch B's KA3/KA4): RADD (KA5): ids 61 (Specify and Model Requirements - fit representation to audience), 62 (Verify Requirements - quality characteristics), 63 (Verify vs Validate distinction), 64 (Define Design Options / recommend by value within constraints), 65 (requirement-design continuum), 66 (Validate Requirements - central question), 67 (reconcile requirements with a design constraint), 68 (design/architecture as components + interactions), 74 (acceptance/evaluation criteria feed later evaluation), 75 (Define Requirements Architecture), 79 (Validate - reconcile conflicting stakeholder value views), 80 (assess potential value / allocate requirements across releases), 81 (choose appropriate modeling format), 84 (traceability to detect unrequested design / scope creep), 85 (stakeholder confirmation of requirements), 87 (design vs requirement characterization), 88 (completeness quality characteristic), 90 (RADD activities that set up objective later evaluation) = 18 items. Solution Evaluation (KA6): ids 69 (Measure Solution Performance), 70 (measures aligned to expected value/goals), 71 (Analyze Performance Measures / Assess Solution Limitations - diagnose before acting), 72 (solution vs enterprise limitation), 73 (Recommend Actions to Increase Solution Value), 76 (actual-vs-expected value comparison - financial), 77 (ROI - financial), 78 (benefit-cost ratio comparison - financial), 82 (interpret variance vs tolerance), 83 (ultimate value benchmark = Strategy Analysis goals/value), 86 (enterprise-limitation recommendation), 89 (ongoing monitoring posture when meeting targets) = 12 items. The three financial items (76,77,78) are embedded in the Solution Evaluation weighting.

FINANCIAL ITEM COUNT COORDINATION: Batch C contributes 3 financial/quantitative calculation items (76 actual-vs-expected value; 77 ROI; 78 benefit-cost ratio). Combined with Batch B's 5 (NPV, IRR, TCO, payback, ROI) the exam-wide running total is 8 financial items across A+B+C, landing in the target ~7-8 range; Batch D need not add more (and Batch A's id22/id23 payback/PV items are additional standard calculation items authored earlier - if the compiled total should stay at 7-8, FEAT-004/FEAT-005 can note that A already carries 2 calc items so the true running calc-item count is higher; Batch C deliberately capped at 3 to avoid overshooting).

PER-BATCH A/B/C/D ANSWER TALLY (Batch C): A=8, B=8, C=8, D=6. Combined with the running total after A+B (A=15, B=17, C=15, D=13) the running total after A+B+C is A=23, B=25, C=23, D=19 across 90 items. Batch D (30 items) should therefore skew its answer keys toward D (about D=11, and lighter on B) to converge on the mock4/mock5-style 30/30/30/30 target at 120; e.g. a Batch D distribution of roughly A=7, B=5, C=7, D=11 would land the compiled exam at A=30, B=30, C=30, D=30.

FINANCIAL ITEMS - WORKED ARITHMETIC AND CONFIRMED ANSWER LETTER (each re-derived independently in python3 via validate_batchC.py; keyed letter provably matches the worked computation):
  * id76 (actual vs expected value): expected annual value = $500,000. Actual = $9,200/week x 50 operating weeks = $460,000. Shortfall = 500,000 - 460,000 = $40,000 (8% below target) -> solution underperforming. Keyed answer C ('$40,000 short'). Distractors: A misreads the figures as a gain, B ignores the gap, D inverts the direction of the difference. Tagged '[verify against your BABOK reference]' because the specific weekly-benefit interpretation is a constructed scenario rather than a fixed BABOK figure.
  * id77 (ROI): net benefit = total benefit - cost = 250,000 - 200,000 = 50,000. ROI = net benefit / cost = 50,000 / 200,000 = 0.25 = 25%. Keyed answer B (25%). Trap distractor C (125%) uses gross benefit (250,000/200,000) instead of net; A (18%) and D (80%) do not follow from the figures.
  * id78 (benefit-cost ratio, COUNTER-INTUITIVE equal-net-benefit trap): Option X BCR = 600,000/400,000 = 1.50; Option Y BCR = 750,000/550,000 = 1.36. Net benefit is identical for both (600,000-400,000 = 200,000; 750,000-550,000 = 200,000), the deliberate trap, but X achieves the same net at lower cost so its ratio is higher. Keyed answer C ('Option X, higher ratio despite equal net benefit'). Distractor A gives the right pick with the wrong reason (ignores equal net), B picks the lower ratio, D ignores the ratio gap. Labeled very difficult.

EVALUATION GATE PASSED (verified item-by-item, programmatically where possible): (a) each item has exactly one defensible BABOK-correct answer and three plausible-but-wrong distractors (no throwaway/absurd options); (b) every stem is self-contained and unambiguous (each calculation stem supplies all figures needed); (c) the batch verifiably hits the ~25/50/25 difficulty mix (8/15/7) after the upward revision of the seven very-difficult items and two difficult promotions - the gate specifically caught and corrected an initial easy drift; (d) every explanation justifies the key AND explicitly rules out the three distractors; (e) every calculation item's worked arithmetic was re-derived in python3 and matches its keyed letter (see above). Schema validation passed in BOTH python3 and node: 30 items, ids 61-90 unique, all choices A-D present, non-empty, and mutually distinct, answer in {A,B,C,D}, non-empty question and explanation. Fixed one authoring slip during the gate (the same slip Batch B recorded): an accidental empty 'E' choice on id69 was removed so the item has exactly four options.

DEDUP CONFIRMATION: dedup_batchC_full.py built a corpus of 1650 existing normalized stems (from js/data/questions.json, BOM-aware utf-8-sig) plus all 30 Batch A stems plus all 30 Batch B stems (1710 total) and reported for batchC.json: 0 exact duplicates, 0 near-duplicates (Jaccard>=0.75), 0 identical-option-set matches, and 0 internal duplicates within Batch C. The highest observed token overlap was Jaccard=0.42 (batchC id73 ~ existing ka6_set2 id46), well below the 0.75 near-dup threshold, so there are no borderline items to iterate on. Net: 0 duplicates vs existing 1650 + 0 vs Batch A + 0 vs Batch B + 0 internal.

HONESTY: all content is original authoring grounded in general BABOK v3 knowledge; no claim of matching any unseen external source. One item (id76) carries a '[verify against your BABOK reference]' tag because its actual-vs-expected value scenario embeds constructed figures rather than a fixed BABOK number; every other item relies on standard BABOK v3 KA5/KA6 concepts (Specify and Model Requirements, Verify Requirements, Validate Requirements, Define Design Options, requirement-design continuum, Define Requirements Architecture, acceptance/evaluation criteria, Measure Solution Performance, Analyze Performance Measures, Assess Solution/Enterprise Limitations, Recommend Actions to Increase Solution Value, and the standard financial techniques ROI/benefit-cost ratio/actual-vs-expected value) that are standard knowledge-area and technique concepts, so no further verify tags were needed.
